test_name: Baseline transthoracic echocardiogram with LVEF and global longitudinal strain
rationale: A documented pre-treatment LVEF is the precondition for giving doxorubicin, and the LMS-04 schedule carries the anthracycline to a cumulative dose that puts a patient into the cardiotoxicity surveillance band (PMID 35835135). ASCO and the 2022 ESC cardio-oncology guideline both call for baseline ventricular imaging, with strain where available, before anthracycline exposure (PMID 27918725; PMID 36017568). Nothing cardiac is on file here, so cycle 1 would otherwise be given with no reference value against which a later fall in function could be read.
tissue_required_estimate: no tissue; transthoracic echocardiogram (5-10 mL blood only if natriuretic peptides are added)
decision_gated: Fitness for doxorubicin in the planned LMS-04 induction, plus the reference LVEF for on-treatment cardiac monitoring.
notes: Performed at the treating institution rather than a send-out laboratory, which is why no provider list is given. Add natriuretic peptide and troponin at the same visit if the cardio-oncology service wants a biochemical baseline. This is the single most time-critical item in the case: induction is planned and not started.

test_name: Baseline comprehensive metabolic panel with bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, transaminases, creatine kinase and calculated creatinine clearance
rationale: Trabectedin dosing and its hepatic dose-modification rules run off bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase and transaminases, and hepatotoxicity plus rhabdomyolysis were the dose-limiting toxicities in the registration trial (PMID 26371143). Doxorubicin is also dose-reduced for hyperbilirubinaemia. No laboratory value of any kind was supplied at intake, so there is currently no baseline against which a treatment-emergent transaminase rise could be interpreted.
tissue_required_estimate: 5-10 mL whole blood (serum chemistry); no tumor tissue
decision_gated: Starting dose and hepatic dose-modification rules for trabectedin in the LMS-04 regimen.

providers.name: Labcorp Oncology
providers.notes: Routine chemistry with the shortest turnaround and the widest draw-site network; either major reference laboratory is equivalent for this panel, so proximity to the patient should decide.

notes: Order creatine kinase alongside the liver tests: trabectedin-associated rhabdomyolysis is monitored on CK, and it is easy to omit from a standard metabolic panel.

test_name: Baseline CBC with differential, reticulocyte count and ferritin, interpreted against an altitude-adjusted haemoglobin reference
rationale: Residence at roughly 8,500 ft raises steady-state haemoglobin by an amount that varies by population and is not captured by sea-level reference ranges (PMID 31257609), so a sea-level-normed CBC will make chemotherapy-induced anaemia look milder than it is and will delay transfusion and dose-modification decisions. Grade 3-4 neutropenia and thrombocytopenia were both common on the doxorubicin plus trabectedin arm of LMS-04 (PMID 35835135), which makes the pre-treatment counts the reference for every subsequent dose decision. No blood count is on file.
tissue_required_estimate: 3-5 mL whole blood (EDTA); no tumor tissue
decision_gated: Dose modification and transfusion thresholds during LMS-04 induction, corrected for chronic high-altitude erythrocytosis.

providers.name: Labcorp Oncology
providers.notes: Standard CBC; the interpretive step, not the assay, is what matters here, so draw locally and record the residence altitude on the requisition.

notes: Record the altitude on the requisition and ask the treating team to state the adjusted reference interval in the chart. If she relocates to sea level for treatment, the baseline will drift downward over weeks for physiological reasons and that drift should not be read as marrow toxicity.

feature: Bilateral pulmonary metastases with an infiltrative, possibly inflammatory radiologic pattern
test_name: Baseline pulmonary function tests with DLCO, plus resting and ambulatory pulse oximetry recorded at residence altitude
rationale: Bilateral infiltrative pulmonary disease in a never-smoker at 8,500 ft needs a measured baseline before induction, because a resting saturation that looks abnormal at sea-level norms may be her physiological steady state, and a saturation that looks acceptable may hide real loss of reserve. The same numbers later decide whether metastasectomy or SBRT is survivable once systemic control is achieved, which the consulting sarcoma oncologist explicitly kept on the table. Without a pre-treatment measurement, any on-treatment desaturation cannot be separated into progression, pneumonitis, or altitude physiology.
tissue_required_estimate: no tissue; spirometry with DLCO and oximetry
decision_gated: Fitness for LMS-04 induction with extensive bilateral lung disease, and the reserve calculation for later metastasectomy or SBRT.
notes: Performed at the treating institution, so no send-out provider list applies. Ask for the oximetry to be recorded at her residence altitude and again at the treating centre if the two differ; a single figure with no altitude attached is close to uninterpretable in this patient.

test_name: Documented clinician-assessed ECOG performance status (with Karnofsky equivalent) recorded at the pre-treatment visit
rationale: The ECOG of 1 carried through this case was assigned at intake as an assumption, not recorded by a clinician, and the intake note says so explicitly. Nearly every sarcoma trial sets an ECOG ceiling of 1 or 2 at screening, so an undocumented score will either stall an application or produce a screen failure after tissue and time have been spent. It is free to fix and should be written into the chart at the same visit as the pre-induction labs.
turnaround_estimate: immediate at the next clinic visit
tissue_required_estimate: no tissue; clinician assessment at the pre-treatment visit
decision_gated: Trial screening eligibility across the sarcoma portfolio, and the fitness call for full-dose LMS-04 induction.
notes: Flagged here because it gates broadly rather than because it is a laboratory test. She is symptomatic with cough and dyspnea yet well enough to travel for specialist consultation, which is consistent with either ECOG 1 or ECOG 2; the difference decides several trial doors. Downstream agents should not treat the current value as measured.

test_name: Tumor NGS covering BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, RAD51C, RAD51D, ATM and the wider HRR gene set, with a reported genomic-instability / LOH score
rationale: Of everything untested here, homologous-recombination status is the entry this histology most earns: olaparib plus temozolomide produced a 27% objective response rate and a median PFS of 6.9 months in pretreated advanced uterine leiomyosarcoma, and 31% of the enrolled patients carried an HRR gene mutation (PMID 37467452). Uterine leiomyosarcoma has a recognised HR-deficient subset including BRCA2 deletion and mutation (PMID 37143137). Skipping it leaves the one non-cytotoxic branch in this case unopened at the point where first-line chemotherapy fails.
tissue_required_estimate: archival FFPE acceptable; the 2024 resection block is preferred for tumor content and volume, with the 2026 lung core held in reserve
decision_gated: Olaparib plus temozolomide (NCI protocol 10250, NCT03880019) and PARP-inhibitor trial entry at progression.

providers.name: Caris Life Sciences
providers.assay_brand: MI Profile (whole exome plus whole transcriptome)
providers.notes: Exome-plus-transcriptome design returns the HRR gene set, genomic LOH, TMB, MSI and RNA fusions off one archival order, which is the bundling this case needs. Preferred over a DNA-only panel because it also closes the NTRK question in the same run.

providers.name: Tempus AI
providers.address: 600 West Chicago Avenue, Suite 510, Chicago, IL 60654

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: Reports HRR genes and a genomic LOH score, but is DNA-only; a separate RNA fusion assay would still be needed.

providers.name: Myriad Genetics
providers.address: 320 Wakara Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108
providers.notes: The genomic-instability score with the best analytical validation, but its threshold of at least 42 was set and validated in ovarian carcinoma, not sarcoma; treat the score as descriptive here rather than as a companion-diagnostic call.

notes: Order the somatic panel and the germline panel together rather than in sequence. On the specimen question, the 2024 resection is the right block: it has more tumor and no intervening systemic therapy separates it from the 2026 disease, so treatment-driven genomic divergence is not a concern in this case.

test_name: RNA-based fusion NGS panel covering NTRK1, NTRK2, NTRK3 (and RET, ALK, ROS1 in the same run)
rationale: This must be an RNA-based assay: NTRK breakpoints sit in large introns and a DNA-only panel misses them, so ordering comprehensive profiling without confirming RNA fusion calling would produce a false negative that reads as a closed question. Prevalence in uterine leiomyosarcoma is very low, but spindle-cell morphology is exactly the setting in which an NTRK-rearranged mesenchymal neoplasm is misclassified, and this tumor was already signed out as a benign leiomyoma once. A positive converts a chemotherapy-only plan into an oral TRK inhibitor with durable response rates.
tissue_required_estimate: archival FFPE acceptable; runs on the same 2024 resection block as the DNA panel, no separate procedure
decision_gated: Larotrectinib, entrectinib or repotrectinib under the tumor-agnostic NTRK fusion indication.

providers.name: Caris Life Sciences
providers.notes: Whole-transcriptome sequencing calls fusions without a fixed breakpoint list and is bundled with the DNA panel already recommended, so no second block cut is needed.

providers.name: Tempus AI
providers.address: 600 West Chicago Avenue, Suite 510, Chicago, IL 60654

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: Includes RNA sequencing for fusions; FoundationOne CDx does not, so the assay must be specified by name when ordering.

notes: Pan-TRK IHC is a screen only and a positive would still need fusion-capable confirmation, so going straight to RNA sequencing avoids a two-step delay. Confirm on the requisition that RNA fusion calling is included; several widely used panels are DNA-only.

test_name: Mismatch-repair protein IHC (MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6), with reflex MLH1 promoter methylation and BRAF V600E if MLH1 is lost
rationale: Four stains on a block that is already being cut close a tumor-agnostic PD-1 indication that would otherwise sit open as a question at progression. Uterine leiomyosarcoma is nearly always mismatch-repair proficient, so a negative is the expected result and the value is in settling it cheaply and early. Loss of any one protein in a woman in her thirties also carries Lynch syndrome implications for her and for first-degree relatives, which is a second reason not to leave it unmeasured.
tissue_required_estimate: archival FFPE; 4-5 unstained slides from either block, bundled with the other IHC in one cut
decision_gated: Pembrolizumab or dostarlimab under the tumor-agnostic MSI-H / dMMR indication, and Lynch syndrome referral.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: Runs the four-stain MMR panel and the other IHC in this case (PD-L1, HER2, B7-H3) as a single accession, which keeps the archival block cut to one pass.

providers.name: Mayo Clinic Laboratories
providers.assay_brand: MMR IHC with reflex MLH1 methylation

providers.name: ARUP Laboratories
providers.address: 500 Chipeta Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108

notes: IHC and PCR/NGS microsatellite testing disagree in a minority of cases; if MMR IHC is intact but clinical suspicion persists, the MSI call off the comprehensive panel is the cross-check. Report MMR IHC and the panel MSI result side by side rather than treating either as definitive alone.

test_name: Validated comprehensive genomic profiling panel reporting TMB in mutations per megabase (with MSI and the BRAF codon 600 call in the same report)
rationale: TMB here is unknown rather than low, because no sequencing of any kind has been performed. Leiomyosarcoma is copy-number driven and usually low-TMB, so a value at or above 10 mut/Mb would be unusual, but the same order returns MSI, BRAF V600E, the HRR genes and the TP53/RB1/ATRX/MED12 backbone, which makes TMB close to free once the panel is placed. Specify a validated comprehensive assay: a TMB figure from a small hotspot panel does not satisfy the tumor-agnostic indication and is not portable between platforms.
tissue_required_estimate: archival FFPE acceptable; same 2024 resection block and same accession as the HRR panel
decision_gated: Pembrolizumab under the tumor-agnostic TMB-H indication (KEYNOTE-158, NCT02628067).

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: The TMB reporting used to define eligibility in the KEYNOTE-158 tumor-agnostic cohort, so a borderline value from this assay is the one least likely to be challenged at trial or payer review.

providers.name: Tempus AI
providers.address: 600 West Chicago Avenue, Suite 510, Chicago, IL 60654

notes: TMB is assay-dependent and a value near the cutoff does not transfer between platforms. If the case is being bundled onto a single Caris or Tempus order for the RNA fusion work, take the TMB from that same report and note the platform in the chart rather than sending a duplicate specimen to a second laboratory.

test_name: Expert sarcoma pathology review of both specimens with formal grading: mitotic index per 10 high-power fields, coagulative tumor cell necrosis, nuclear atypia, FNCLCC grade, plus an assessment of whether the 2024 block was adequately sampled
tissue_type: archival FFPE, both the September 2024 resection and the 2026 lung core
rationale: The diagnosis itself has now been confirmed by a reference laboratory, but the parameters that drive prognosis and trial eligibility (mitotic count, coagulative necrosis, grade) are not on file, and a 6.0 cm myometrial mass handled as a benign leiomyoma in 2024 was very unlikely to have been sampled at the one block per centimetre standard applied to a suspected sarcoma. Major diagnostic revisions occur in a quarter of sarcoma cases sent for expert second opinion (PMID 33061792), and this case has already produced one. Without documented grade and mitotic index, several trial screening forms cannot be completed and the prognostic conversation rests on assumption.
tissue_required_estimate: archival FFPE blocks and slides from both specimens; additional levels may be cut from the 2024 block, which will consume tissue
decision_gated: Formal grade and mitotic index for prognosis and for trial screening forms; also settles whether the 2024 block needs deeper levels.

providers.name: MD Anderson Cancer Center, Department of Pathology
providers.notes: High-volume sarcoma pathology consultation with a dedicated gynecologic sarcoma practice; chosen over the other academic consult services because uterine leiomyosarcoma grading sits at the intersection of the two subspecialties.

providers.name: Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, Department of Pathology

notes: Order the additional levels and the grading review before the block is exhausted by the molecular orders. Sequence matters: agree the tissue allocation across pathology review, the NGS panel and the IHC set in one conversation rather than three separate requisitions.

test_name: HLA class I genotyping at 4-digit (allele-level) resolution
rationale: Every HLA-restricted agent that could reach this patient names its restricting allele, most often HLA-A*02:01, so without a genotype the PRAME and MAGE-A4 rows sit as unassessable rather than negative. It is a blood draw that spends no tumor tissue and costs little, and the result either opens the TCR-T and ImmTAC class for later consideration or closes it cleanly. Ordering it now avoids a two-step delay if she progresses through first-line chemotherapy while a trial slot is open.
tissue_required_estimate: 5-10 mL whole blood (ACD or EDTA) or a buccal swab; no tumor tissue consumed
decision_gated: PRAME, MAGE-A4 and NY-ESO-1 directed TCR-T and ImmTAC programs, all of which are allele-restricted.

providers.name: Histogenetics
providers.notes: High-volume dedicated HLA laboratory with routine allele-level class I typing and a short turnaround, which is what the cell-therapy programs ask for; the general reference labs will do it but often at lower resolution unless specified.

providers.name: ARUP Laboratories
providers.address: 500 Chipeta Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108
providers.assay_brand: HLA class I typing, high resolution

notes: Specify allele-level (4-digit) resolution on the requisition; a 2-digit serologic type will not satisfy a cell-therapy screening form. Draw it on the same visit as the germline HR panel so one venipuncture covers both.

test_name: B7-H3 (CD276) IHC on tumor tissue
tissue_type: archival FFPE; the 2024 resection preferred for its larger sampled area
rationale: B7-H3 carries the best odds of a positive result of any surface target in this histology: 97% of soft tissue sarcomas stained positive and about 69% were high in a 153-patient series across 15 subtypes (PMID 39478506). Nothing is approved against it, so a positive buys trial access rather than a prescription, but the ADC and bispecific programs generally require documented expression at screening and a later referral should not stall while tissue is hunted down. Expression is spatially heterogeneous, which argues for reading the larger resection rather than the core alone.
tissue_required_estimate: archival FFPE; 2-3 unstained slides, bundled into the same block cut as the MMR, PD-L1 and HER2 stains
decision_gated: Screening access to B7-H3-directed ADC, bispecific and CAR-T programs; trial-only, with no approved agent in this class.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: Offers B7-H3 as a custom or laboratory-developed stain alongside the routine IHC in this case; scoring is not standardised between sponsors, so treat the result as a screening signal rather than a portable score.

providers.name: Discovery Life Sciences
providers.notes: Runs B7-H3 IHC as a research-use assay; useful when a trial specifies its own antibody clone.

providers.name: MD Anderson Cancer Center, Department of Pathology
providers.notes: Academic sarcoma pathology laboratories will often run the stain on request when a specific trial referral is in play.

notes: No standardised clinical scoring system exists for B7-H3, so a locally generated result may still need repeating on the sponsor's own assay at screening. Worth doing anyway: a negative here would spare a futile referral, and a strong positive is the most likely surface-target finding in this case.

feature: ER and PR <1% by IHC (decision-relevant negative)
test_name: Retrieval of the ER and PR IHC report: specimen of origin (2024 uterine resection versus 2026 lung core), antibody clone, scoring system and internal control adequacy
tissue_type: existing report and stained slides; no new tissue unless the slides cannot be located
rationale: ER and PR are recorded as confirmed at <1%, and that negative closes a door which is genuinely open in this histology: letrozole met its activity criterion in ER and/or PR-positive uterine leiomyosarcoma, with the longest PFS in tumors staining strongly and diffusely (PMID 24222211). Before a foreclosure of that weight is relied on, the report should state which specimen was stained, which clone was used and whether the internal control worked, because a failed stain on an old block reads identically to a true negative at the <1% cutoff. This is a records step rather than a new assay, and it costs nothing but a phone call.
tissue_required_estimate: no new tissue; existing report and stained slides retrieved from the originating laboratory
decision_gated: Whether the endocrine foreclosure holds, and therefore whether aromatase inhibition stays off the option list.

providers.name: MD Anderson Cancer Center, Department of Pathology
providers.notes: If the slides are re-read rather than merely retrieved, send them with the sarcoma pathology consultation already recommended rather than opening a separate accession.

notes: The point is not to doubt the result but to know what it is a result about. If the stain was run on the 2024 primary, the paired row below applies; if it was run on the 2026 lung core with working controls, the endocrine door is closed on current disease and no further receptor testing is warranted.

test_name: TP53, RB1, ATRX and MED12 status from the comprehensive tumor NGS panel
rationale: These four genes are the mutational backbone of uterine leiomyosarcoma on exome sequencing (PMID 26891131) and they ride along free on the panel already being ordered for HRR, TMB and MSI. ATRX loss in particular tracks with the alternative lengthening of telomeres phenotype, aggressive histology and shorter survival in leiomyosarcoma (PMID 25229770), so it feeds the prognostic conversation and the urgency of the treatment plan. None of the four is directly druggable today, which is why this is a high rather than an essential row.
tissue_required_estimate: no additional tissue; reported from the same 2024 resection accession as the HRR and TMB panel
decision_gated: Prognostic framing and biological classification; informs trial matching but gates no current agent.

providers.name: Caris Life Sciences
providers.notes: Same accession as the HRR and fusion work; no separate order or specimen is required.

providers.name: Tempus AI
providers.address: 600 West Chicago Avenue, Suite 510, Chicago, IL 60654

notes: Worth reading alongside the grading review: concordant TP53 and RB1 loss with a high mitotic index paints a consistent high-grade picture, and a discordant result would be a prompt to revisit the classification.

feature: ~23-month interval between resection of the primary (September 2024, signed out benign) and correct diagnosis (July-August 2026)
test_name: Retrieval of the September 2024 operative report and gross pathology description: route of hysterectomy, whether power or manual morcellation was used, specimen integrity and margin status
tissue_type: no tissue; operative and gross pathology records
rationale: A 6.0 cm myometrial mass removed as a presumed benign fibroid in 2024 may have been morcellated, and morcellation of an unrecognised leiomyosarcoma disperses tumor through the peritoneum and has been linked to worse outcomes (PMID 28209496; PMID 26646120). The current staging picture is pulmonary only; if the specimen was disrupted, peritoneal and pelvic disease has to be actively excluded rather than assumed absent. The answer sits in an operative note that nobody has yet had reason to re-read.
tissue_required_estimate: no tissue; operative note and gross description from the September 2024 hysterectomy
decision_gated: Whether peritoneal and pelvic disease must be actively excluded, and how the staging imaging field is drawn.
notes: Records retrieval rather than a send-out assay, hence no provider list. Pair the request with the pathology block release so one letter to the 2024 institution covers both.

feature: ~23-month interval between resection of the primary (September 2024, signed out benign) and correct diagnosis (July-August 2026)
test_name: Pre-treatment CT chest, abdomen and pelvis with measurable RECIST target lesions, read against any imaging from the September 2024 to July 2026 interval
rationale: Induction has not started, so there is still a clean window to fix a pre-treatment baseline with named target lesions; once cycle 1 is given, that window is gone and response assessment becomes an argument about which prior scan counts. Any imaging from the 23-month interval would bound the growth rate of the pulmonary disease, which is the closest thing available to a measure of tempo in a systemic-therapy-naive patient. The infiltrative, possibly inflammatory appearance also needs to be documented before treatment, because it will complicate the reading of every subsequent scan.
tissue_required_estimate: no tissue; contrast-enhanced CT, with prior outside imaging requested on disc
decision_gated: RECIST baseline for LMS-04 response assessment and for any subsequent trial screening; also bounds disease tempo.
notes: Performed locally, so no provider list applies. Ask specifically for outside imaging from the 2024 to 2026 interval on disc rather than for the reports alone; the measurements matter more than the narrative.

test_name: Germline multigene hereditary cancer panel including BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, RAD51C, RAD51D, ATM, TP53 and the Lynch genes
rationale: A germline result matters twice over here: it settles whether any somatic HRR finding is inherited, and at 39 with a high-grade sarcoma it carries direct implications for her siblings, children and any future pregnancy decisions. Uterine leiomyosarcoma is part of the Li-Fraumeni tumor spectrum, so TP53 belongs on the panel rather than being inferred from a somatic result. Somatic-only testing leaves this open, which is why the blood panel should go out alongside the tumor panel rather than as a reflex after it.
tissue_required_estimate: 5-10 mL whole blood (EDTA); drawn on the same visit as HLA typing
decision_gated: Cascade testing for relatives, Li-Fraumeni surveillance if TP53 is positive, and germline confirmation of any somatic HRR finding for PARP-inhibitor trial screening.

providers.name: Myriad Genetics
providers.address: 320 Wakara Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108
providers.notes: Broad hereditary cancer panel with established insurance pathways and integrated genetic counselling, which matters for a patient who will need cascade testing arranged for relatives.

notes: Pair the order with formal genetic counselling; a TP53 finding in a 39-year-old changes surveillance for the whole family and should not arrive as an unheralded line on a report.

feature: ER and PR <1% by IHC (decision-relevant negative)
test_name: Repeat ER and PR IHC on the 2026 pulmonary metastasis core, reported with percentage and intensity rather than a binary call
rationale: If the <1% result came off the 2024 uterine primary, it describes a specimen taken 23 months and one metastatic step away from the disease being treated, and hormone receptor expression in uterine leiomyosarcoma is not uniformly retained between primary and metastasis. The letrozole trial selected on ER and/or PR positivity and found the longest PFS in strongly and diffusely positive tumors (PMID 24222211), so the question worth answering is not positive versus negative but whether any meaningful expression exists on current disease. If the original stain was already run on the lung core with working controls, skip this row.
tissue_required_estimate: archival FFPE; 2 unstained slides from the 2026 lung core, added to the same block cut as the other IHC
decision_gated: Whether aromatase inhibition re-enters the option list as a later-line or maintenance-phase choice.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: Bundle with the MMR, PD-L1, HER2 and B7-H3 stains already going to one laboratory so the lung core is cut once.

notes: Conditional on the provenance row above. The lung core is a small specimen and every stain spends it, so this only earns its place if the original receptor result came from the 2024 primary. Endocrine therapy would not displace the planned induction in any case; the question is what is available afterwards.

test_name: PRAME IHC on archival tissue, ordered only if HLA class I typing returns a restricting allele
rationale: PRAME cannot be called in either direction right now, because neither the antigen nor the restricting HLA allele has been tested. Sequence the two: if HLA typing returns A*02:01, PRAME IHC gates entry to the ImmTAC and TCR-T programs, and if it does not, this row closes with no tissue spent. Reported PRAME expression in leiomyosarcoma runs below the levels seen in synovial sarcoma, so a negative stain would not be surprising.
tissue_required_estimate: archival FFPE; 2 unstained slides, ideally from the 2024 resection to preserve the lung core
decision_gated: PRAME-directed ImmTAC and TCR-T programs (brenetafusp, IMA203); trial-only, and conditional on HLA type.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: Carries PRAME on its routine IHC menu and can hold the order pending the HLA result.

notes: Sponsors run their own companion assays at screening, so a local result is a screening step rather than a substitute. Order PRAME and MAGE-A4 as one antigen set on a single block cut rather than as two requisitions.

test_name: MAGE-A4 IHC on archival tissue, ordered only if HLA class I typing returns a restricting allele
rationale: MAGE-A4 stays unknown until the HLA type is back, since the whole class is allele-restricted. Even a positive stain would not make her eligible for afamitresgene autoleucel, which was studied and licensed in synovial sarcoma and myxoid round cell liposarcoma rather than in sarcoma generally (PMID 38554725), so the realistic destination is a MAGE-A4 solid-tumor TCR-T trial of the kind run across histologies in HLA-A*02-positive patients (PMID 36624315). Stain it in the same antigen set as PRAME rather than as a separate order.
tissue_required_estimate: archival FFPE; 2 unstained slides from the same cut as the PRAME stain
decision_gated: MAGE-A4-directed TCR-T trials (SURPASS programme); trial-only for this histology, and conditional on HLA type.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: Same accession and same block cut as the PRAME stain, which is the only sensible way to order a two-antigen reflex.

notes: Reported MAGE-A4 expression in leiomyosarcoma runs below the levels seen in synovial sarcoma, where this antigen class was developed; I could not find an indexed leiomyosarcoma-specific expression series, so treat the prior probability as low but not quantified. Companion-diagnostic testing for the approved product runs on the sponsor's own assay, so a local IHC result is useful for deciding whether a referral is worth making, not for satisfying eligibility.

test_name: RAD51 foci immunofluorescence assay for functional homologous-recombination deficiency
rationale: In NCI protocol 10250 the RAD51 functional assay, not the mutation list, was what separated outcomes: median PFS was 11.2 months in homologous-recombination-deficient tumors versus 5.4 months in proficient ones (PMID 37467452). That makes it the most direct read on whether this tumor would benefit from olaparib plus temozolomide, and it can be positive in tumors with no HRR gene mutation. Clinical availability is the problem: it is largely an academic and research assay with no widely offered CLIA version, which is why this ranks medium rather than essential.
tissue_required_estimate: archival FFPE; feasibility should be confirmed with the receiving laboratory before slides are cut
decision_gated: Refines the olaparib plus temozolomide decision beyond HRR mutation status; supplements rather than replaces the somatic panel.

providers.name: Discovery Life Sciences
providers.notes: Research-services route for the assay. I could not identify a major US reference laboratory offering a CLIA-validated RAD51 foci assay as a catalogue test, so treat access as trial-linked or academic collaboration rather than orderable.

providers.name: MD Anderson Cancer Center, Department of Pathology
providers.notes: Academic sarcoma programs running PARP-inhibitor studies are the realistic access point; ask whichever centre holds the trial slot.

notes: Do not hold up the somatic HRR panel waiting for this. If a PARP-inhibitor trial is the destination, ask the site whether it runs or requires the functional assay before spending slides on it independently.

test_name: ATRX IHC on both the September 2024 primary and the 2026 pulmonary metastasis
rationale: Paired sequencing of both blocks was floated and is not worth the cost here: no systemic therapy was given in the 23-month interval, so there is no treatment-driven selection pressure to have produced genomic divergence, and the 2024 resection has the tumor content the panel needs. Paired ATRX IHC is the cheap version of the same question, and ATRX loss with the ALT phenotype tracks with aggressive histology and shorter survival in leiomyosarcoma (PMID 25229770). Two stains on blocks already being cut will show whether the primary is representative of the metastatic disease.
tissue_required_estimate: archival FFPE; 1-2 unstained slides from each block, bundled with the other IHC
decision_gated: Whether the 2024 primary is representative of the 2026 metastatic disease; prognostic rather than treatment-selecting.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: Runs ATRX as part of its routine sarcoma and glioma IHC menu, and can take both blocks on one accession.

providers.name: ARUP Laboratories
providers.address: 500 Chipeta Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108

notes: This is where I part company with the bundled proposal: paired NGS on both blocks buys little in a systemic-therapy-naive patient, whereas paired ATRX IHC answers the representativeness question for the price of two stains. Read it against the ATRX call from the NGS panel; discordance between the two would itself be informative.

feature: Bilateral pulmonary metastases with an infiltrative, possibly inflammatory radiologic pattern
test_name: PD-L1 IHC with the clone and scoring system matched to the intended agent, plus CD3 and CD8 T-cell infiltrate density, on the 2026 pulmonary metastasis core
rationale: PD-L1 gates no approval in soft tissue sarcoma, so this informs rather than decides, and the results that would actually open checkpoint blockade for her are MSI and TMB. It earns a row because the pulmonary lesions were read as infiltrative and possibly inflammatory, and someone will ask whether that appearance reflects an immune infiltrate or tumor growth pattern; a CD3 and CD8 read on the lung core answers that directly.
